newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGUESE REFEREE FOUND GUILTY IN BRIBE CASE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGUESE REFEREE FOUND GUILTY IN BRIBE CASE.

text.p: A former Portuguese referee and the chairman of a first division soccer club were sentenced to jail on Wednesday for bribery.

Referee Jose Guimaro, who told journalists that he would appeal, was given 15 months after being convicted by a court in the northern city of Matosinhos of accepting money to influence the outcome of matches.
The current chairman of the Leca soccer club, Manuel Lopes Rodrigues, was sentenced to one year in prison, while two other men were given sentences of eight months.
All four denied the charges which stemmed from a 1993 investigation into match-rigging.
The court case came at a delicate time for Portuguese soccer with the domestic game shaken by a series of allegations of bribery and attempts to influence referees.

UEFA, European soccer's governing body, is to probe allegations that Portuguese champions Porto sought to bribe a referee 12 years ago before an European Cup Winners' Cup match with Scotland's Aberdeen.

Both Porto and the Romanian referee who had charge of the game in 1984 have denied the accusations but UEFA decided to investigate given the seriousness of the allegations made by a Portuguese businessman, who says he acted as go-between.
Porto are also at the centre of another controversy over a holiday in Brazil for referee Carlos Calheiros in the summer of 1995.
The club has officially admitted that it picked up the 700,000 escudo ($4,600) bill for the holiday but says that it did so without realising who it was for.
Guimaro, 41, was arrested in June 1994 after months of investigations in which police searched the homes of several referees and club directors.
The case came to be known as the "case of the 500,000" after police found photocopies of a cheque for half a million 500,000 escudos ($3,300) in Guimaro's house.
The prosection charged that the money was part of a two million escudo ($13,200) payment made by Lopes Rodrigues to Guimaro to favour Leca which at the time was a second division club.
